system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

## How I've treated the package

- **I have reviewed every clause, including those marked [STANDARD].** The seller's labels ("cleared by both sides", "FINAL", "not intended to be re-opened", "market standard", "agreed at principal level") are assertions by the other side. Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, they don't clear anything for us. Only our own authority process can.
- **Several seller numbers resemble our fallbacks** (20% cap, 18-month period). A fallback is conditional. The 20% cap requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and the 18-month period requires her written approval. Neither has been given, so neither can be conceded.
- **The facts are stale.** The disclosure letter speaks as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Every fact needs a bring-down.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only with Frost authority | Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Restore AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Reject. Restore 24 months. |
| Limitation cascade | Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" | No hidden general-regime override | Reject. Each regime stands separately. |
| Title/capacity | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject. Restore the separate Fundamental regime. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, to the maximum enforceable extent, non-waivable | Reject. Add the fraud carve-out. |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete general disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes matters known to Buyer/advisers or discoverable in data room/public records | Delete blanket exclusion; qualifiers need named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Delete 8.3 or narrow it to the playbook test. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3; DL §2) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Make it a pre-Completion condition. The DL confirms no final consent. Revenue at risk is about AUD 3.6m (~30%). |
| Riverlark (2/7; DL §3) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Reject. The DL confirms about AUD 3.2m outstanding and no discharge. |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL §5) | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them | Reject. Add as a specific line item or make it seller-funded, including on-costs. On-costs are not quantified in the DL. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1; DL §4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not verified either way | Reject. Broaden the indemnity. Verify the AUD 180,000 independently in either direction. |
| DD-006 export/privacy (4.6/Sch 6; DL §6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Reject the materiality characterisation. Neither accept nor assert breach. Require logs, scope and updates. Any specific protection needs deal-team and Frost decisions. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Reject the characterisation. The DL says the nature is not stated. Assess on the facts. |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Reject. Keep Tax and IP as separate open categories. |
| Title (DL §10) | DD-012 share register as evidence of title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source only | Reject. Require independent title searches and encumbrance evidence. |

## Material issues and reasoning

1. **Liability architecture.** The seller's package moves every key term against us at once: a lower cap, a higher de minimis, a higher basket with excess-only recovery, a shorter period, and a cascade that drags Title and Tax into the general regime. Together, a typical claim under the seller's terms could be largely unrecoverable.

2. **Fraud carve-out missing.** The seller's limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses expressly apply to "all Claims of any nature". The playbook treats the fraud carve-out as non-waivable, so this is a hard point.

3. **Deemed disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Whole data-room disclosure combined with an 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion would shift risk of anything in the data room to us. This is a combined risk, not two separate ones.

4. **Consent and debt conditions.** Bluefen and Riverlark are both fully open per the DL. The seller's "satisfied on delivery" and "release after Completion" approaches would close without them resolved.

5. **Funds flow.** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are excluded from the funds flow and labelled as "a matter for the Seller". That's a funds-flow gap that needs fixing before signing.

6. **Items the seller's draft doesn't address.** The DL flags a Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) and an office lease notification obligation (DD-007). Neither is addressed in the seller's update. The DL says neither is stated to require consent for the share sale. We should confirm this with counsel rather than accept it.

## Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the seller's package as drafted.** Do not accept any [STANDARD] label as cleared.
2. **Restore playbook positions:** 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month general period, and a separate Fundamental/Title regime (100%, at least 6 years).
3. **Add a non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
4. **Replace general and deemed disclosure** with specific fair disclosure. Delete the 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion, or narrow it to the playbook test.
5. **Make Bluefen a pre-Completion condition** requiring effective consent and evidence the conditions are satisfied.
6. **Require Riverlark payout from Completion funds** and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
7. **Fix the funds flow** to include the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs as a specific line item, or make them seller-funded.
8. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** and preserve the SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
9. **Investigate DD-006.** Require preservation of logs, the investigation scope and regular updates. Don't characterise it as a breach or as immaterial.
10. **Assess the Sandbar renewals** on the facts. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
11. **Keep Tax and IP open** and separate. Don't accept "settled under the general regime".
12. **Require independent title evidence.** DD-012 is not independent proof.
13. **Bring the disclosure current** to the Completion date and confirm the Mossvale and office lease position with counsel.
14. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** any proposal to concede the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Those need her written authority identifying the draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
